claims.text: Aging CoCrFeNiAl at approximately 600 °C for 4 hours followed by air cooling will form fine nanoscale L12 precipitates.
The aging-induced L12 precipitates will be coherent and homogeneously dispersed throughout the matrix.
L12 precipitates obstruct dislocation motion through their strengthening characteristics.
The aging treatment will increase yield strength relative to the untreated or solution-treated baseline.
The aging treatment will improve mechanical durability relative to the untreated or solution-treated baseline.
The L12 precipitates will reduce room-temperature creep by impeding deformation mechanisms.
The aged alloy will have a lower room-temperature creep rate than the untreated or solution-treated alloy.
L12 precipitates act as nucleation sites for the formation of a stable passive oxide film.
The precipitate-promoted passive film will improve corrosion resistance.
The aged alloy will exhibit lower corrosion current density or higher pitting potential than the untreated or solution-treated baseline.
As-cast or solution-treated CoCrFeNiAl has a relatively coarse microstructure.
The untreated or solution-treated baseline typically has lower mechanical strength than the proposed aged state.
The untreated or solution-treated baseline typically has higher room-temperature creep rates than the proposed aged state.
The untreated or solution-treated baseline typically has inferior corrosion protection compared with the proposed aged state.
The proposed benefits will hold under room-temperature aerospace-fastener service conditions.
Changes in alloy composition or service temperature can alter the treatment outcomes.
Additional heat treatment can coarsen L12 precipitates.
Insufficiently optimized aging parameters may cause embrittlement.
